_comment: Handler permissions the execution policies deliberately do not allow. `permission` is an fnmatch pattern (case-insensitive). Each entry needs a reason. Reviewed with the handler snapshot.

omissions.reason: No VPC-attached Lambda in the stacks (VPC describe calls are only for VPC configs).
No EFS file system config on any function.
No S3 Files mount on any function.
No customer-managed KMS key in the stacks; all encryption uses service-owned keys.
No customer-managed KMS key on log groups.
No customer-managed KMS key on log groups.
No Kinesis stream; the table does not stream.
No Kinesis streaming destination on the table.
No Kinesis streaming destination on the table.
No Kinesis streaming destination on the table.
No autoscaling on the on-demand table.
Lambda capacity providers are not used.
Runtime aliases are not used.
No Lambda layers are used (container images).
Log delivery to S3 or Firehose is not used.
No S3 code, OpenAPI body or log delivery in the stacks (Lambda code is a container image).
Log delivery to Firehose is not used.
Needed only for cross-region table replicas; the table has no replicas.

GlobalTable update handler uses it only for replica removal. The explicit deny on ai-radar-cards stays; the table is RETAIN with no replicas, so a future replica removal is a manual step outside the execution role.
GlobalTable update handler uses it only for replica removal. The table has no replicas; a future replica removal is a manual step outside the execution role (same reason as DeleteTable).
No IAM groups in the stacks.
The caller user has no console password.
Permissions boundaries are out of scope (execution plan, follow-up risk).
No cross-region secret replication.
No cross-region secret replication.
